A1.justification: Both PDFs contain readable main text and appendices for the same TRecViT study. Equations, tables, figures, and retained experiments can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, point-tracking, video-memorisation, sequence-length generalisation, and efficiency results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds component ablations, broader baseline comparisons, hyperparameter sweeps, and a five-seed experiment.

M1.justification: The reported temporal Conv1D window changes from 2 in v1 Section 3.3 to 4 in v2 Section 3.2 and Table 14. The time-space-channel architecture, recurrence equations, and MAE objective remain unchanged. Newly documented skip connections do not establish that this component was newly introduced.

E1.justification: Both versions retain ImageNet pretraining, Kinetics400 and SSv2 classification, MOVi-E training with DAVIS/Perception Test tracking evaluation, and Walking Tours reconstruction and length generalisation. Additional clip lengths and ablations vary settings within this coverage. Video diffusion and variable-frame-rate applications remain future work.

E2.justification: v2 Tables 3–4 substantially expand classification comparisons, including TSM, RViT, causal ViViT, and additional convolutional, transformer, and Mamba baselines. ViViT-B is removed from the SSv2 comparison but retained for Kinetics400. Table 2 adds ViT-LSTM, ViT-Conv1D, and factorised self-attention comparisons; efficiency plots also add factorised ViViT variants.

E3.justification: v2 adds a 64-frame SSv2 classification configuration alongside the original 32-frame setting, trains causal ViViT with attention masks, and introduces controlled patch-duration, convolution-window, and eigenvalue-range sweeps. The no-skip ablation also uses a reduced learning rate. Existing MAE and point-tracking schedules are retained.

E4.justification: v2 Section 5.1 and Appendix D add quantified ablations of skip connections, gates, convolution, alternative temporal modules, temporal patch size, kernel width, and eigenvalue initialisation. These substantially extend v1's reported design choices and analyses. The earlier memorisation, length-generalisation, and tracking visualisations are largely retained through relocation or merging.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix D first reports five SSv2 seeds with a result of 66.6 ± 0.2 and discloses that the best seed, seed 0, supplies the comparison result and other experiments. v1 supplies neither run counts nor uncertainty estimates, so an increase over its actual run count cannot be established.

E6.justification: The reported TRecViT Kinetics400 accuracy changes from 78.4% in v1 Table 2 to 76.5% in v2 Table 4. SSv2 retains the 32-frame result of 66.8% and adds 68.2% with 64 frames. Numerous baseline, ablation, and efficiency entries are added. Frozen-MAE classification and point-tracking scores remain unchanged; revised model configuration limits controlled cross-version performance interpretation.

T1.justification: v2 Section 4.2 adds a computational derivation comparing full attention's O(LT^2N^2D + LTND^2) cost with TRecViT's O(LTN^2D + LTND^2), extending v1's brief scaling statements. The stability discussion also removes the earlier suggestion that stability prevents vanishing gradients. The recurrence equations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: v2 newly claims the first causal architecture in the video SSM family, state-of-the-art SSv2 performance among causal models, and real-time inference at approximately 300 frames per second. v1 claimed competitive performance and efficiency without these priority, causal-SOTA, or throughput claims. v2 also explicitly ties the headline efficiency savings to full self-attention ViViT.

C2.justification: v2 adds hypotheses linking temporal-first processing and smaller temporal patches to simpler, more continuous LRU inputs. It qualifies efficiency advantages against factorised ViViT and explains the factorised encoder's restriction to sparse tasks. The conclusion replaces the scaling-focused discussion with future investigations of memorisation, video diffusion, and variable frame rates.

D1.justification: v2 Table 8 explicitly documents Small/Base/Large layer counts, hidden dimensions, MLP sizes, and attention heads; Figure 1's caption clarifies skip connections. Comparison tables add pretraining metadata. Most training hyperparameters and the code/checkpoint access information already existed in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds a dedicated causal-video discussion, identifies RViT as the closest work, and positions TRecViT as the first causal video SSM. Related work expands to streaming models and newer recurrent architectures, including Mamba 2, Gated Delta Networks, and MesaNet. This substantially changes positioning beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: v2 moves LRU background into related work, reorganises experiments into ablations and SOTA comparisons, merges memorisation with length generalisation, and redistributes existing discussion into lettered appendices. The introduction and conclusion are substantially revised around causal modelling.

P2.justification: The paper changes from two-column to single-column layout. Classification tables expand and separate causal from non-causal models, efficiency plots are redrawn with additional curves, and new ablation/configuration tables appear. Existing tracking panels are merged, while memorisation and generalisation figures move into the appendix.

improvement.justification: The causal and factorised comparisons, component ablations, and seed reporting strengthen architectural evidence that was limited in v1. However, v2 revises Kinetics400 accuracy from 78.4% to 76.5% while Section 5.2 still claims to outperform ViViT-B at 78.1%; the new approximately 300-fps claim also lacks timing conditions. These reporting inconsistencies limit the overall quality gain.
